content.text:
The biggest risk was your release binaries, not any library. Every `wt` you've shipped was built with **go1.24.0** from February 2025, so it lacks about 20 months of security fixes to Go's standard library. I've fixed that, patched the one library CVE, and left nothing uncommitted except the changes below.

**What was wrong**
- `release.yml` and `ci.yml` asked for Go 1.22. Since `go.mod` says `go 1.24.0`, Go quietly downloaded exactly 1.24.0 and built with that. I confirmed it: `go version /opt/homebrew/bin/wt` prints `go1.24.0`.
- That also means the CI test matrix (1.22 and 1.23) never tested what it claimed. Both legs ran on 1.24.0.

**Changes (not committed)**
- **Workflows:** release, build and lint now use `go-version: stable`. The test matrix is `["1.26", "stable"]`. golangci-lint goes from v2.1 to v2.15, because v2.1 can't lint Go 1.26 code.
- **`golang.org/x/sys`:** 0.36.0 → 0.49.0. This fixes GO-2026-5024, an integer overflow that only affects Windows. You don't ship Windows builds, so it never reached anyone.
- **Patch-level bumps:** the other dependencies got patch updates, and `go mod tidy` moved bubbletea and lipgloss to direct deps, since `internal/tui` imports them. The `go` line in `go.mod` is now 1.26.0, because the new x/sys requires it.
- Build, tests, vet and lint all pass. After the upgrades, govulncheck finds no library vulnerabilities.

**Still open**
- **GO-2026-6809:** a `crypto/x509` fix that needs Go 1.27.3 or later. Your local Go is 1.27.2, so run `brew upgrade go`. CI's `stable` setting will pick up the fix on its own.
- **Ship a release:** the Homebrew binaries stay vulnerable until you tag one. Run `/wt-release` once this is committed.

I did not take the minor version bumps (`fatih/color` 1.19 and so on), because nothing requires them. The `charmbracelet/x/ansi` package jumped from 0.10 to 0.11 as a side effect, and `internal/tui` has no tests, so open `wt dash` once before you release.
